proposer_argument.content:
POSITION
Claim B provides the stronger, more specific, and technically authoritative statement, though Claim A correctly identifies the underlying phenomenon.

EVIDENCE REVIEW
Claim A: The retrieved evidence supports that the loop area represents hysteresis loss occurring each magnetization cycle, describing the phenomenon in general energetic terms without dimensional precision.
Claim B: The retrieved evidence supports that the loop area represents energy dissipated as heat, specifically quantified per unit volume per cycle, matching the standard integral form of the B-H loop with proper physical units.

REASONING
The core issue is dimensional specificity rather than conceptual disagreement. The area enclosed in a B-H hysteresis loop has units of energy per unit volume, so describing it solely as energy loss per cycle omits the necessary volumetric qualifier and is quantitatively incomplete. Claim B includes both the heat dissipation mechanism and the correct per-unit-volume normalization, making it more precise and aligned with authoritative physics formulations. Claim A is conceptually valid but less specific.

SOURCE BASIS
Only sources or evidence present in the supplied claims and standard electromagnetic loop-area interpretations referenced therein.

CONCLUSION
Resolve in favor of Claim B: the area enclosed by a hysteresis loop measures the energy dissipated as heat (hysteresis loss) per unit volume per cycle, with Claim A representing the same idea lacking the required volumetric specificity.
